claim: Fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe are rod-shaped cells that grow to ∼14 µm in length before entering mitosis.
source: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe are rod-shaped cells that grow to ∼14 µm in length before entering mitosis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is consistent with established knowledge about S. pombe cell biology.

claim: Cells enter mitosis at a certain surface area, as opposed to a certain volume or length.
source: We show that cells enter mitosis at a certain surface area, as opposed to a certain volume or length.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6, showing that cells with different shapes divide at similar surface areas but different volumes and lengths.

claim: Cdr2p is a peripheral membrane protein kinase that has properties of a dose-dependent 'sizer' that controls mitotic entry.
source: A peripheral membrane protein kinase cdr2p has properties of a dose-dependent 'sizer' that controls mitotic entry.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing that varying cdr2p expression levels affects cell size at division in a dose-dependent manner.

claim: As cells grow, the local cdr2p concentration in nodes at the medial cortex accumulates as a measure of cell surface area.
source: As cells grow, the local cdr2p concentration in nodes at the medial cortex accumulates as a measure of cell surface area.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 2 and 6 showing that cdr2p intensity at nodes increases with cell length and correlates with surface area rather than volume.

claim: During interphase, fission yeast cells grow from the cell tips at a nearly constant rate to approximately 14 µm in length before entering mitosis.
source: During interphase, these cells grow from the cell tips at a nearly constant rate to approximately 14 µm in length before entering mitosis, when cell growth ceases until the next cell cycle (Mitchison and Nurse, 1985).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by Mitchison and Nurse, 1985.

claim: The DYRK kinase pom1p is an inhibitor of the SAD family kinase cdr2p.
source: Genetic analyses in fission yeast have identified a pathway of conserved protein kinases for cell size control: the DYRK kinase pom1p is an inhibitor of the SAD family kinase cdr2p, which inhibits wee1p, which in turn inhibits the cell division kinase cdk1p (Russell and Nurse, 1987; Breeding et al., 1998; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: Cdr2p inhibits wee1p.
source: Genetic analyses in fission yeast have identified a pathway of conserved protein kinases for cell size control: the DYRK kinase pom1p is an inhibitor of the SAD family kinase cdr2p, which inhibits wee1p, which in turn inhibits the cell division kinase cdk1p (Russell and Nurse, 1987; Breeding et al., 1998; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: Wee1p inhibits the cell division kinase cdk1p.
source: Genetic analyses in fission yeast have identified a pathway of conserved protein kinases for cell size control: the DYRK kinase pom1p is an inhibitor of the SAD family kinase cdr2p, which inhibits wee1p, which in turn inhibits the cell division kinase cdk1p (Russell and Nurse, 1987; Breeding et al., 1998; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: Loss of function of pom1 leads to abnormally short cells.
source: Loss of function of pom1 and wee1 leads to abnormally short cells, whereas loss of function of cdr2 leads to abnormally long ones.
evidence: This is consistent with established knowledge about these mutants and is supported by the genetic pathway described.

claim: Loss of function of wee1 leads to abnormally short cells.
source: Loss of function of pom1 and wee1 leads to abnormally short cells, whereas loss of function of cdr2 leads to abnormally long ones.
evidence: This is consistent with established knowledge about these mutants and is supported by the genetic pathway described.

claim: Loss of function of cdr2 leads to abnormally long cells.
source: Loss of function of pom1 and wee1 leads to abnormally short cells, whereas loss of function of cdr2 leads to abnormally long ones.
evidence: This is consistent with established knowledge about these mutants and is supported by the genetic pathway described.

claim: Pom1p localizes in cortical gradients emanating from cell tips.
source: Pom1p localizes in cortical gradients emanating from cell tips (Bahler and Pringle, 1998; Padte et al., 2006; Hachet et al., 2011; Saunders et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies and is confirmed by imaging data in Figure 1.

claim: Cdr2p localizes to a medial band of plasma membrane protein complexes termed 'nodes', which overlie the medial nucleus.
source: Cdr2p localizes to a medial band of plasma membrane protein complexes termed 'nodes', which overlie the medial nucleus (Morrell et al., 2004; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and is confirmed by imaging data in Figure 2.

claim: Wee1p, Cdk1p, and other regulators of mitotic entry localize primarily to the spindle pole body and nucleus.
source: Wee1p, Cdk1p, and other regulators of mitotic entry localize primarily to the spindle pole body and nucleus (Alfa et al., 1990; Masuda et al., 2011; Grallert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pom1p cortical gradients exhibit large cell-to-cell variability in intensity and distribution.
source: Pom1p cortical gradients exhibit large cell-to-cell variability in intensity and distribution, fluctuate over time in individual cells, and show little consistent change with cell length (Saunders et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Saunders et al., 2012 and is consistent with data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Pom1p cortical gradients fluctuate over time in individual cells.
source: Pom1p cortical gradients exhibit large cell-to-cell variability in intensity and distribution, fluctuate over time in individual cells, and show little consistent change with cell length (Saunders et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Saunders et al., 2012.

claim: Pom1p cortical gradients show little consistent change with cell length.
source: Pom1p cortical gradients exhibit large cell-to-cell variability in intensity and distribution, fluctuate over time in individual cells, and show little consistent change with cell length (Saunders et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Saunders et al., 2012 and is confirmed by data in Figure 1B,C,D.

claim: Measurements of pom1-tomato at the medial cortex showed no detectable decrease with cell length in a population of cells.
source: Importantly, measurements of pom1-tomato at the medial cortex showed no detectable decrease with cell length in a population of cells (Figure 1B), or in individual cells imaged over time (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Measurements of pom1-tomato at the medial cortex showed no detectable decrease with cell length in individual cells imaged over time.
source: Importantly, measurements of pom1-tomato at the medial cortex showed no detectable decrease with cell length in a population of cells (Figure 1B), or in individual cells imaged over time (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Pom1-3GFP produces a consistently steeper gradient profile than pom1-GFP or pom1-tomato fusions.
source: Pom1-3GFP (pom1p fused to three tandem GFPs) produced a consistently steeper gradient profile than pom1-GFP or pom1-tomato fusions (Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: There were no differences in cell length at division between pom1-3GFP, pom1-GFP, and pom1-tomato strains.
source: However, we detected no differences in cell length at division between these pom1-tagged strains (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G,H.

claim: There were no significant differences in the intensities or number of cdr2p nodes between pom1-3GFP and pom1-GFP strains.
source: Consistent with this result, there were no significant differences in the intensities or number of cdr2p nodes (Figure 1—figure supplements 4C, 5).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 4C, 5.

claim: Cdr2-GFP concentration in the whole cell remained approximately constant in interphase cells of various lengths.
source: Cdr2-GFP concentration in the whole cell remained approximately constant in interphase cells of various lengths (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The intensity of cdr2-GFP at the medial cortex increased with cell length.
source: Interestingly, the intensity of cdr2-GFP at the medial cortex increased with cell length (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplements 2, 3).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and supplementary figures.

claim: The local cdr2p concentration in the medial cortex region rises approximately twofold as cells grow through interphase.
source: Measurement of cdr2-GFP intensity within a 3-μm wide region of the medial cortex showed directly that the local cdr2p concentration in this region rises approximately twofold as cells grow through interphase (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mature cdr2p nodes contain an average of ∼90 cdr2-GFP molecules.
source: Mature cdr2p nodes, estimated to each contain an average of ∼90 cdr2-GFP molecules (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), moved very slowly and exhibited little change over hours (Video 1).
evidence: This is based on quantitative fluorescence measurements described in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cdr2-GFP turned over with a t1/2 of about 3 min within each node.
source: FRAP studies, however, revealed that cdr2-GFP turned over with a t1/2 of about 3 min within each node (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is directly supported by FRAP experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: With increasing cell length, the number of nodes in each cell increased.
source: With increasing cell length, the number of nodes in each cell increased (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 5A), whereas the intensities of individual nodes remained unchanged (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 5A.

claim: The intensities of individual cdr2p nodes remained unchanged with increasing cell length.
source: With increasing cell length, the number of nodes in each cell increased (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 5A), whereas the intensities of individual nodes remained unchanged (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 5B.

claim: Mild cdr2p overexpression (estimated 1.6-fold) caused cells to divide at abnormally short cell lengths.
source: Mild cdr2p overexpression in the absence of thiamine (estimated 1.6-fold) caused cells to divide at abnormally short cell lengths.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Higher levels of cdr2p overexpression caused cytokinesis defects and accumulation of longer cells.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Breeding et al., 1998), higher levels of overexpression caused cytokinesis defects and accumulation of longer cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work and is consistent with experimental observations.

claim: Decreased cdr2p expression led cells to divide at much longer lengths, similar to a cdr2 null strain.
source: Conversely, decreased cdr2p expression led cells to divide at much longer lengths, similar to a cdr2 null strain (Morrell et al., 2004; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and is consistent with experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: The majority of cdr2p is highly stable in interphase cells.
source: The persistence of cdr2-GFP in cells treated with the protein synthesis inhibitor cyclohexamide showed that the majority of cdr2p is highly stable in interphase cells (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D,E using cycloheximide treatment.

claim: Latrunculin A-treated cells exhibited no growth and no increase in cdr2-GFP levels at nodes.
source: Latrunculin A-treated cells exhibited no growth and no increase in cdr2-GFP levels at nodes (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The rate of cdr2-GFP accumulation at nodes strongly correlated with the rate of cell growth in for3Δ mutants.
source: The rate of cdr2-GFP accumulation at nodes strongly correlated with the rate of cell growth. (p<10−3 see 'Materials and methods'; Figure 4C,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cdr2p localizes to dim, dynamic dots all around the cortex in addition to nodes and cytoplasmic haze.
source: In further characterizing the dynamic behavior of cdr2p, we found that in addition to cdr2p in nodes and a diffuse cytoplasmic haze, it also localized to dim, dynamic dots all around the cortex (Figure 5A, Video 2).
evidence: This is directly supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5A and Video 2.

claim: The distribution of dim cortical cdr2-GFP dots did not vary over the cell tip and did not correlate with levels of pom1p at cell tips.
source: Interestingly, the distribution of these dim cortical cdr2-GFP dots did not vary over the cell tip, and thus did not correlate with levels of pom1p at cell tips.
evidence: This is based on observations from imaging data in Figure 5A.

claim: Cdr2p is able to bind to the whole surface of the cell.
source: Thus, cdr2p is able to bind to the whole surface of the cell.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of dim cortical cdr2p dots distributed around the entire cell cortex.

claim: In pom1Δ mutants, cdr2-GFP is spread in dots throughout much of the cortex, except for the growing cell tip.
source: In pom1Δ cells, cdr2-GFP is spread in dots throughout much of the cortex, except for the growing cell tip (Figure 7A; Celton-Morizur et al., 2006; Padte et al., 2006; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and is confirmed by imaging data in Figure 7A.

claim: The total amount of cdr2p in the cell was similar in wild-type and pom1Δ mutant cells over a range of cell lengths.
source: The total amount of cdr2p in the cell was similar in wild-type and pom1Δ mutant cells over a range of cell lengths (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In pom1Δ cells, cdr2p was still enriched over the medial cortex.
source: Cortical profiles showed that in pom1Δ cells, cdr2p was still enriched over the medial cortex and that the non-growing end had levels roughly half that of the medial region (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The fraction of cdr2p that is cortical and the area of nodal cdr2p were both substantially increased in pom1Δ cells.
source: The fraction of cdr2p that is cortical and the area of nodal cdr2p were both substantially increased in pom1Δ cells (Figure 7D,E).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D,E.

claim: The increase of cortical cdr2p with cell length was similar in pom1Δ vs wild-type cells, but the curve was shifted slightly upwards.
source: Interestingly, the increase of cortical cdr2p with cell length was similar in pom1Δ vs wild-type cells, but the curve was shifted slightly upwards (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: In the medial cortical region of pom1Δ cells, cdr2p levels were lower than wildtype.
source: In contrast, in the medial cortical region, cdr2p levels were lower than wildtype (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Cdr2p nodes are more motile in pom1Δ cells than in WT.
source: Time-lapse imaging showed that cdr2p nodes are more motile in pom1Δ cells than in WT (Figure 7H; Videos 1, 3), suggesting a defect in the anchoring of these nodes in the membrane.
evidence: This is directly supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 7H and Videos 1, 3.

claim: In a group of interphase cells of similar surface area but of different volumes, nodal cdr2-GFP intensities correlated with surface area.
source: In a group of interphase cells of similar surface area but of different volumes, nodal cdr2-GFP intensities correlated with surface area (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B using rga2Δ and rga4Δ mutants with different cell widths.

claim: In cells of similar volume but with a range of different surface areas, cdr2-GFP nodal intensity correlated with surface area and not volume.
source: Conversely, in considering cells of similar volume but with a range of different surface areas, cdr2-GFP nodal intensity correlated with surface area and not volume (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C using rga2Δ and rga4Δ mutants with different cell widths.

claim: Cells with different shapes entered mitosis with more similar cell surface areas but differing cell volumes and lengths.
source: These cells with different shapes entered mitosis with more similar cell surface areas but differing cell volumes and lengths (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E comparing wild-type, rga2Δ and rga4Δ strains.

claim: All three strains (wild-type, rga2Δ, rga4Δ) exhibited average surface areas of 150 µm2 ± 8 µm2 at division.
source: All three strains exhibited average surface areas of 150 µm2 ± 8 µm2, while the average volumes varied from 120 µm3 to 150 µm3 and average lengths from 11 µm to 15 µm.
evidence: This is based on measurements from experimental data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: The distributions of surface area at division were more similar than those for volume or length across different cell shapes.
source: A more rigorous analysis based on Jensen–Shannon distances ('Materials and methods') showed quantitatively that the distributions of surface area were more similar than those for volume or length.
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 6E using Jensen-Shannon distances.

claim: Pom1p may exert its cell size effects in part by ensuring the proper localization of cdr2p nodes to the medial region.
source: Pom1p may exert its cell size effects in part by ensuring the proper localization of cdr2p nodes to this region (Celton-Morizur et al., 2006; Padte et al., 2006; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009) (see below).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and is consistent with the experimental observations in Figure 7.

claim: Cells can, in principle, control their size by growing to a specified size before commencing cell division.
source: Cells can, in principle, control their size by growing to a specified size before commencing cell division.
evidence: This is a general statement about cell size control mechanisms based on established knowledge.

claim: How any cell actually senses its own size remains poorly understood.
source: How any cell actually senses its own size remains poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: In several cell types, cells have been shown to have a size threshold, in which they need to grow to a minimal cell size before committing to cell division.
source: In several cell types, cells have been shown to have a size threshold, in which they need to grow to a minimal cell size before committing to cell division (Turner et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Turner et al., 2012.

claim: The molecular mechanism for how size is sensed, and what aspect of size—surface area, volume, mass, linear dimensions etc—is monitored remains unknown.
source: The molecular mechanism for how size is sensed, and what aspect of size—surface area, volume, mass, linear dimensions etc—is monitored remains unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe is an attractive eukaryotic model for cell size studies because of its highly regular dimensions, simple rod-shape, and growth patterns.
source: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe is an attractive eukaryotic model for cell size studies because of its highly regular dimensions, simple rod-shape, and growth patterns.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about S. pombe as a model organism.

claim: A current model for cell size control is based on pom1p concentration gradients as 'rulers' to sense cell length.
source: A current model for cell size control is based on pom1p concentration gradients as 'rulers' to sense cell length (Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009; Vilela et al., 2010; Tostevin, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies proposing this model.

claim: The gradient model postulates that as cells grow in length from their tips, pom1p gradients are moved away from cdr2p nodes at mid-cell, causing decreased pom1p levels at the medial cortex.
source: This gradient model postulates that as these cells grow in length from their tips, pom1p gradients are moved away from cdr2p nodes at mid-cell, causing decreased pom1p levels at the medial cortex.
evidence: This is a description of the previously proposed gradient model.

claim: Core assumptions of the previous pom1p gradient model are not consistent with experimental findings.
source: We find that core assumptions of the previous pom1p gradient model are not consistent with experimental findings.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1 showing that pom1p levels at the medial cortex do not decrease with cell length.

claim: Cells sense their size by using cdr2p to probe the surface area over the whole cell and relay this information to the medial cortex.
source: Our findings, which challenge a previously proposed pom1p gradient model, lead to a new model in which cells sense their size by using cdr2p to probe the surface area over the whole cell and relay this information to the medial cortex.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data and mathematical modeling throughout the manuscript.

claim: The localization of a cdr2p sizer at cortical nodes allows the local concentration of nodal cdr2p to increase as the cell grows.
source: The localization of a cdr2p sizer at cortical nodes provides several key advantages over other locales. First, it allows the local concentration of nodal cdr2p to increase as the cell grows.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in Figure 2 and is explained through mathematical modeling.

claim: Nuclear volume increases as cells grow in fission yeast.
source: Previously proposed mechanisms have been based upon nuclear concentration or the nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of a sizer, but in many cell types (including fission yeast), nuclear volume also increases as cells grow (Neumann and Nurse, 2007; Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Neumann and Nurse, 2007 and is confirmed by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Medial cortical placement of nodes surrounding the medial nucleus may allow cdr2p to communicate its local concentration to presumed targets such as wee1p and cdk1p on the nucleus.
source: Second, we speculate that medial cortical placement of nodes surrounding the medial nucleus may allow cdr2p to communicate its local concentration to presumed targets such as wee1p and cdk1p on the nucleus.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the known localizations of these proteins.

claim: Wee1p localization in late G2-phase is in the nucleus and at the spindle pole body (SPB).
source: Although wee1p can be observed at some nodes upon overexpression (Moseley et al., 2009), its localization in late G2-phase is clear in the nucleus, and at the spindle pole body (SPB) (Masuda et al., 2011), a structure on the nuclear envelope situated close (often <0.5 μm) to the nodes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cdk1/cyclin B and polo kinase are located at the SPB and nucleus.
source: Cdk1/cyclin B and polo kinase are also located at the SPB and nucleus (Alfa et al., 1990; Masuda et al., 2011; Grallert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The SPB could detect local gradients of cdr2p (or other molecules) emanating from nearby cortical nodes.
source: Potentially, the SPB could detect local gradients of cdr2p (or other molecules) emanating from nearby cortical nodes.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about how cdr2p might signal to cell cycle regulators.

claim: Additional layers of regulation such as through phosphorylation states or diffusion barriers would be needed to generate suitably steep gradients from cdr2p.
source: However, as a simple cdr2p concentration gradient in the cytoplasm is expected to be very shallow (due to rapid diffusion), it is likely that additional layers of regulation such as through phosphorylation states or diffusion barriers would be needed to generate suitably steep gradients.
evidence: This is based on inference from the known properties of diffusion and the need for effective signaling.

claim: The localization of nodes to the medial cortical region involves multiple inputs.
source: The localization of these nodes to the medial cortical region involves multiple inputs.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations and known factors affecting node localization.

claim: A primary role of pom1p may be to ensure the medial localization of nodes.
source: Although pom1p clearly regulates cdr2p function and phosphorylation, our data indicate that the pom1p gradient distribution may not be the primary size sensing mechanism as previously proposed. Indeed, our data are consistent with a recent report that size correction still occurs in pom1Δ mutants (Wood and Nurse, 2013). Rather, a primary role of pom1p may be to ensure the medial localization of nodes.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in Figure 7 and is supported by a citation to Wood and Nurse, 2013.

claim: Pom1p may affect cdr2p nodes in part by affecting distribution and general properties (such as its mobility in the membrane) of the nodes.
source: Thus, pom1p may affect cdr2p nodes in part by affecting distribution and general properties (such as its mobility in the membrane) of the nodes.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in Figure 7 showing altered cdr2p distribution and mobility in pom1Δ cells.

claim: Cdr2p activity is regulated by phosphorylation by pom1p and ssp1p protein kinases.
source: Recent studies (published while this work was in press) suggest that cdr2p activity is also regulated by phosphorylation by pom1p and ssp1p protein kinases (Bhatia et al., 2014; Deng et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies by Bhatia et al., 2014 and Deng et al., 2014.

claim: The nucleus governs dynamic nodal localization, in a mechanism that may involve nuclear shuttling.
source: Studies on mid1p, another component of the nodes, suggest that the nucleus governs dynamic nodal localization, in a mechanism that may involve nuclear shuttling (Paoletti and Chang, 2000; Daga and Chang, 2005; Almonacid et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on mid1p.

claim: The organization of the cortical endoplasmic reticulum influences nodal stability and localization.
source: Furthermore, the organization of the cortical endoplasmic reticulum also influences nodal stability and localization (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: There are likely to be additional (or alternative) inputs into size control beyond cdr2p.
source: There are also likely to be additional (or alternative) inputs into size control (Coudreuse and Nurse, 2010; Navarro and Nurse, 2012; Wood and Nurse, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies identifying other factors involved in size control.

claim: Additional cell size regulators include the cell tip protein nif1p.
source: Additional cell size regulators include the cell tip protein nif1p (Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Wood and Nurse, 2013), and skb1p, which localizes to cortical patches distinct from the nodes (Deng and Moseley, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Skb1p localizes to cortical patches distinct from the nodes.
source: Additional cell size regulators include the cell tip protein nif1p (Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Wood and Nurse, 2013), and skb1p, which localizes to cortical patches distinct from the nodes (Deng and Moseley, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Deng and Moseley, 2013.

claim: Cells expressing a cdk1p–cyclinB fusion still exhibit apparently near-normal size control in the absence of wee1p/mik1p or cdk1p-tyrosine phosphorylation control.
source: Cells expressing a cdk1p–cyclinB fusion still exhibit apparently near-normal size control in the absence of wee1p/mik1p or cdk1p-tyrosine phosphorylation control (Coudreuse and Nurse, 2010; Navarro and Nurse, 2012; Wood and Nurse, 2013), suggesting the existence of controls that are entirely independent of cdk1–tyrosine phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: This simple cdr2p-based mechanism is likely to be a core component of a larger network responsible for cell size control.
source: Thus, this simple cdr2p-based mechanism is likely to be a core component of a larger network responsible for cell size control.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings and the known complexity of cell size control.

claim: The mathematical model reveals how the cdr2p dynamics ensure a nodal cdr2p density that scales with cell size, or more specifically, with the surface area of the plasma membrane.
source: Importantly, the model reveals how the cdr2p dynamics ensure a nodal cdr2p density that scales with cell size, or more specifically, with the surface area of the plasma membrane (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on mathematical modeling described in the manuscript and shown in Figure 5.

claim: The area of the nodal region must not scale proportionally with the total cell membrane area as the cell size increases for cdr2p to function as a size sensor.
source: The first is that the area of the nodal region must not scale proportionally with the total cell membrane area as the cell size increases (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a key requirement identified by the mathematical model and is confirmed by experimental data in Figure 2C.

claim: The nodal region receives information via cdr2p about the entire surface area of the cell.
source: The second key element is that the nodal region receives information via cdr2p about the entire surface area of the cell.
evidence: This is a key principle identified by the mathematical model and supported by experimental observations.

claim: Cdr2p needs to be able bind the membrane long enough to move on the membrane to reach the nodal region.
source: In this model, cdr2p needs to be able bind the membrane long enough to move on the membrane to reach the nodal region.
evidence: This is a requirement of the mathematical model for cdr2p to function as a size sensor.

claim: Wild-type S. pombe cells are rod-shaped and have an approximately constant width, so that surface area and cell length are proportional to one another.
source: Note that wild-type S. pombe cells are rod-shaped and have an approximately constant width, so that surface area and cell length are proportional to one another.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about S. pombe cell morphology.

claim: The size-sensing model shares elements with a proposed microtubule length control mechanism termed the 'antenna model'.
source: This size-sensing model shares elements with a proposed microtubule length control mechanism termed the 'antenna model'. In the microtubule model, longer microtubules bind more motor proteins, which then accumulate at the microtubule end in a length-dependent manner (Varga et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison to a previously proposed model, supported by a citation to Varga et al., 2006.

claim: The whole surface area of the plasma membrane may be regarded as an 'antenna' in the cell size sensing mechanism.
source: In the cell size sensing case, the whole surface area of the plasma membrane may be regarded as an 'antenna'.
evidence: This is an analogy used to explain the mechanism of size sensing.

claim: The property of cdr2p to first bind to the plasma membrane 'antenna' is critical for this mechanism to read out cell size.
source: Similar to the microtubule model, the property of cdr2p to first bind to the plasma membrane 'antenna' (as opposed to merely binding the nodes directly) is critical for this mechanism to read out cell size.
evidence: This is a key principle of the proposed mechanism based on the mathematical modeling.

claim: The system is effectively in a dynamic steady state at a given cell size, with fast cdr2p dynamics compared to the timescales of cell growth.
source: Furthermore, as the amount of nodal cdr2p reflects cell size rather than time, we postulate that the system is effectively in a dynamic steady state at a given cell size, with fast cdr2p dynamics compared to the timescales of cell growth.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observation that cdr2p does not accumulate without cell growth (Figure 4) and is a key assumption of the mathematical model.

claim: Size correction still occurs in pom1Δ mutants.
source: Indeed, our data are consistent with a recent report that size correction still occurs in pom1Δ mutants (Wood and Nurse, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wood and Nurse, 2013.

claim: Cdr2p is a stable protein that is synthesized to maintain a constant concentration in the whole cell as the cell grows.
source: Together, these findings suggest that as the cell grows, cdr2p is a stable protein that is synthesized to maintain a constant concentration in the whole cell, and accumulates at the medial cortex, where it promotes mitotic entry in a concentration-dependent manner (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing cdr2p stability (Figure 3D,E) and constant whole-cell concentration (Figure 2B).

claim: Cdr2p accumulates at the medial cortex and promotes mitotic entry in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Together, these findings suggest that as the cell grows, cdr2p is a stable protein that is synthesized to maintain a constant concentration in the whole cell, and accumulates at the medial cortex, where it promotes mitotic entry in a concentration-dependent manner (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing dose-dependent effects of cdr2p on cell size (Figure 3) and accumulation at the medial cortex (Figure 2).

claim: Cdr2p has properties of a 'sizer' not a 'timer'.
source: Thus, cdr2p has properties of a 'sizer' not a 'timer'.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing that cdr2p accumulation depends on cell growth rather than time (Figure 4).

claim: Pom1p is excluded from the nucleus.
source: These cortical measurements improve on previously reported pom1p measurements that integrate intensities over the whole cell (Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009), which have artifacts stemming from the normal exclusion of pom1p from the nucleus (Saunders et al., 2012; Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2,3).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Saunders et al., 2012 and is shown in Figure 1A and supplementary figures.

claim: Rga2Δ mutants are thinner than wild type.
source: Rga2p and rga4p are Rho-GAPs involved in regulation of cell polarity and width (Das et al., 2007; Villar-Tajadura et al., 2008; Kelly and Nurse, 2011); rga2Δ mutants are thinner while rga4Δ mutants are fatter than wild type (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and is shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Rga4Δ mutants are fatter than wild type.
source: Rga2p and rga4p are Rho-GAPs involved in regulation of cell polarity and width (Das et al., 2007; Villar-Tajadura et al., 2008; Kelly and Nurse, 2011); rga2Δ mutants are thinner while rga4Δ mutants are fatter than wild type (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and is shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Nodal cdr2p scales with cell surface area.
source: These results thus suggest that nodal cdr2p scales with cell surface area, in agreement with the predictions of the mathematical models.
evidence: This is based on experimental data in Figure 6B,C using cells with different widths.

claim: Cells monitor their size at the G2/M transition by measuring their surface area.
source: These findings suggest that cells monitor their size at the G2/M transition by measuring their surface area.
evidence: This is based on experimental data in Figure 6 showing that cells with different shapes divide at similar surface areas.

claim: In cells expressing PMT-Pom1C fusion (pom1p targeted all over the plasma membrane), cdr2p was evenly distributed all over the cortex at a low level.
source: A construct in which pom1p is targeted all over the plasma membrane has been described (PMT-Pom1C fusion, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A) (Moseley et al., 2009). Although cdr2p was expressed at normal levels in the whole cell, it was evenly distributed all over the cortex at a low level, and did not increase at the medial cortex with increasing cell length (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Moseley et al., 2009 and is shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells expressing PMT-Pom1C divided at abnormally long cell lengths, similar to cdr2Δ mutants.
source: As shown previously (Moseley et al., 2009), these cells divided at abnormally long cell lengths, similar to cdr2Δ mutants.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Moseley et al., 2009.

claim: Pom1p has an inhibitory effect on cdr2p localization to nodes.
source: These data show that pom1p has an inhibitory effect on cdr2p localization to nodes.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in Figure 7 showing altered cdr2p distribution in pom1Δ and PMT-Pom1C cells.

claim: Cdr2p needs to be present at medial nodes in order to function effectively in cell size control.
source: These results further provide support that cdr2p needs to be present at these medial nodes in order to function effectively in cell size control.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations showing that disruption of medial node localization leads to cell size defects.

claim: The timescale of cell growth (hours) is much slower than the timescale of the cdr2p dynamics (minutes).
source: As the timescale of cell growth (hours) is much slower than the timescale of the cdr2p dynamics (minutes, Figure 2—figure supplement 4), we assumed that the molecular system is, at any given time, effectively in steady state.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing cdr2p turnover time (Figure 2—figure supplement 4) and known cell growth rates.

claim: The steady-state assumption for the mathematical model is consistent with experimental findings that cdr2p levels at nodes are stable over time when cells are not growing.
source: This steady-state assumption is also consistent with experimental findings that cdr2p levels at nodes are stable over time when cells are not growing (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: For3Δ mutants are defective in cell polarity regulation and exhibit highly variable growth rates.
source: We used for3Δ (formin) mutants, which are defective in cell polarity regulation and exhibit highly variable growth rates (Feierbach and Chang, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Feierbach and Chang, 2001.

claim: There are approximately 9000 cdr2p molecules per cell.
source: Quantification of average cdr2p molecules in the whole cell was estimated by comparing total cell fluorescent intensity of cdr2-GFP with rlc1-GFP (regulatory light chain of myosin), which has been estimated around 9600 molecules/cell (Wu and Pollard, 2005) (n = 50 cells).
evidence: This is based on quantitative fluorescence measurements described in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.
